chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥamzah al-ʿAlawī, may Allah have mercy on him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from a number [of narrators], that they heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would not perform prayer during the daytime until the sun had passed the meridian, nor during the night after he had performed the ʿIshāʾ prayer until the middle of the night.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, Commander of the Faithful.
key_terms.تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ: The sun passes the meridian; midday begins after zenith.

ai.seo_question: When did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام perform or avoid supererogatory prayers during the day and night?
ai.summary: This hadith states the practice of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding the timing of supererogatory prayers in the day and night. It indicates specific periods in which he would refrain from performing such prayers, making it relevant to rulings on the times of nawāfil.
